title: 蓝色 LED：3.3 V 还是 5 V？
summary: 蓝色 LED 的压降约 3 V，用 3.3 V 供电几乎没有余量。选对电源模块的电压。
description: 蓝色 LED 的正向压降约 3.0 V。电源模块可以选 3.3 V 或 5 V：3.3 V 只给电阻留 0.3 V，电流很小又不稳；5 V 给电阻留 2 V，用 100 Ω 得到合适的电流。电路：+5 V → 100 Ω → 蓝色 LED → GND。

cards.title: 先试 3.3 V
text: 这一题没有步骤，**照目标电路图自己搭**。搭好后，先在电源模块的「属性」里选 **3.3 V**，看蓝灯有多亮；再换成 **5 V**。

cards.title: 电压余量（headroom）
text: - 限流电阻能稳住电流，靠的是它两端有**足够的电压**。
- 3.3 V 时电阻只分到 $3.3 - 3.0 = 0.3$ V：电流小，而且 LED 的压降稍微大一点点，电流就会大幅变化，甚至完全不亮。
- 5 V 时电阻分到 2 V：$R = \frac{5 - 3.0}{0.02} = 100$ Ω，亮度合适也稳定。

cards.title: 选 5 V，量电流
text: - 选中电源模块，把电压设成 **5 V**。
- 搭好后单击 LED，读电流；再把模块临时改成 3.3 V 对比一下。

cards.title: 带走
text: - 白光、蓝光、绿光（部分）LED 的压降约 3 V：**3.3 V 电源点它们很勉强**。ESP32 这类 3.3 V 单片机直接驱动蓝灯时要特别小心。
- 规律：**电源电压要比 LED 压降高出一截**，留给电阻去稳住电流。

caption.text: 都按 20 mA 设计：5 V 时电阻有 2 V 余量，LED 压降差一点电流几乎不变；3.3 V 时只剩 0.3 V，压降稍大一点电流就掉一大截。

i18n.en: Both designed for 20 mA: at 5 V the resistor has 2 V of headroom and a slightly different LED barely changes the current; at 3.3 V only 0.3 V is left and a slightly higher LED voltage cuts the current hard.

en.title: Blue LED: 3.3 V or 5 V?
en.summary: A blue LED drops about 3 V, so 3.3 V leaves almost no headroom. Pick the right power-module voltage.
en.description: A blue LED has a forward voltage of about 3.0 V. The power module offers 3.3 V or 5 V: 3.3 V leaves only 0.3 V for the resistor, giving a small and unsteady current; 5 V leaves 2 V, and 100 Ω gives a sensible current. Circuit: +5 V → 100 Ω → blue LED → GND.
hints: Click the power module and set its voltage to 5 V in Properties.
tests: Blue LED on, module at 5 V

cards.title: Try 3.3 V first
text: No steps here — **build it from the target schematic**. Then choose **3.3 V** in the power module's Properties and see how bright the blue LED is; then switch to **5 V**.

cards.title: Headroom
text: - A current-limiting resistor can only hold the current steady if it has **enough voltage across it**.
- At 3.3 V the resistor gets just $3.3 - 3.0 = 0.3$ V: little current, and a tiny change in the LED's drop changes the current a lot — or the LED doesn't light at all.
- At 5 V the resistor gets 2 V: $R = \frac{5 - 3.0}{0.02} = 100$ Ω, bright enough and steady.

cards.title: Choose 5 V, measure the current
text: - Click the power module and set it to **5 V**.
- Then click the LED and read its current; switch the module to 3.3 V for a moment to compare.

cards.title: Take away
text: - White, blue and some green LEDs drop about 3 V: **a 3.3 V supply barely lights them**. Take care when a 3.3 V microcontroller like the ESP32 drives a blue LED directly.
- Rule: **the supply should sit well above the LED drop**, leaving voltage for the resistor to steady the current.

measurements.ask: Module at 5 V: click the LED — the current in Properties
Switch the module to 3.3 V: the LED current
measurements.explain: (3.3 − 3.0) / (100 + 12) ≈ 2.7 mA: about a seventh of the 5 V current.
